title: HANAFI RULINGS
entries: Obligatory. In Hanafi law, a fard duty is established by decisive evidence; deliberately leaving it is sinful.
Required in Hanafi law, but established by evidence that is less decisive than fard. Deliberately leaving it is sinful.
An emphasized Sunnah that the Prophet regularly practiced. Habitually neglecting it without excuse is blameworthy.
A practice taught or modeled by the Prophet. Following it is rewarded.
Recommended. Doing it is rewarded; leaving it is not sinful.
Permitted or neutral. The act is allowed in itself.
Mildly disliked. Avoiding it is better and rewarded; doing it is not treated like a prohibited act.
Prohibitively disliked in Hanafi law. It must be avoided and deliberately doing it is sinful.
Forbidden. Deliberately doing it is sinful.

title: PURIFICATION TERMS
entries: Purity or purification, including ritual purity and removal of physical impurity.
The minor ritual washing required for salah and certain other acts of worship.
A full ritual bath required after major ritual impurity and in certain other situations.
Dry purification using clean earth or a qualifying earth-like substance when water cannot be used.
Physical impurity, such as urine or blood, that must be removed when required for worship.
A state of ritual impurity that requires wudu or ghusl. It is not the same thing as physical dirt.
An excused person under Hanafi law whose chronic condition continuously causes something that would normally break wudu.
Cleaning the private areas after using the toilet.
Wiping with wet hands, such as wiping part of the head during wudu.

title: SALAH TERMS
entries: One complete unit of salah, containing its prescribed standing, recitation, bowing, prostrations, and other actions.
Recitation, especially recitation of the Qur’an in salah.
Saying “Allahu Akbar.” The opening takbir begins the prayer.
Prostration in salah, with the forehead and nose placed on the ground along with the required limbs.
The testimony recited while sitting in salah, beginning with al-Tahiyyat.
The greeting that ends the prayer, turning to the right and left.

title: PEOPLE & PRACTICE
entries: The person leading the congregational prayer.
A person praying behind and following an imam.
A latecomer who joins the imam after missing part of the congregational prayer.
The call announcing that the time for an obligatory prayer has entered.
The second call given immediately before the congregational obligatory prayer begins.
The person who gives the adhan.
The direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah, toward which Muslims face in salah.
Intention in the heart to perform an act of worship.
A formal sermon, such as the sermon delivered before the Jumu‘ah prayer.

title: HANAFI STUDY WORDS
entries: The understanding and study of practical Islamic rulings and how they apply.
A disciplined school and method of Islamic law. The Hanafi madhhab is one of the four major Sunni schools.
Relating to the school of Islamic law associated with Imam Abu Hanifa and developed by his students and later jurists.
A legal answer or opinion given by a qualified scholar in response to a religious question.
A qualified scholar who gives fatwas.
Qualified scholarly effort used to derive or determine a ruling from the Islamic sources.
Legal analogy: applying a known ruling to a new case because they share a legally relevant cause.
Scholarly consensus. It is one of the recognized sources used in Islamic legal reasoning.
The principles and methods used to understand the legal sources and derive rulings from them.

title: COMMON ISLAMIC TERMS
entries: Supplication: directly asking Allah for help, forgiveness, guidance, or any good.
Remembrance of Allah through words, recitation, praise, and other acts of remembrance.
Repentance: turning back to Allah, leaving the sin, regretting it, and sincerely intending not to return to it.
Consciousness of Allah that leads a person to obey Him and guard against sin.
Voluntary charity given for the sake of Allah.
Obligatory charity due on qualifying wealth when its conditions are met.
The minimum qualifying amount of wealth used in determining whether zakat is due.
Voluntary worship beyond what is obligatory or required.

title: FOUNDATIONAL TERMS
entries: Allah’s revealed Book sent to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
A verse of the Qur’an. The word also means a sign.
A transmitted report about the Prophet’s words, actions, approvals, or descriptions.
A hadith grading meaning sound or authentic. It is also used in the titles Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
The testimony of faith: none is worthy of worship except Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
A mosque; literally a place of prostration.
A supplication meaning roughly “O Allah, answer.” It is said after al-Fatihah and is not part of the Qur’an.
Qur’an 2:255, commonly called the Verse of the Throne.

title: RECITATION & DHIKR WORDS
entries: The opening praise recited near the beginning of salah after the opening takbir.
Seeking refuge in Allah from Shaytan, beginning A‘udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim.
Saying Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim: “In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.”
Glorifying Allah, especially with phrases such as SubhanAllah. The word is also used for repeated praises in prayer.
Prayers and blessings sent upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
Seeking Allah’s forgiveness, such as by saying Astaghfirullah.
Relying upon Allah while still taking the lawful means available to you.
A special supplication. In this deck it mainly refers to the du‘a recited in the third rak‘ah of Hanafi Witr.

title: SALAH REPAIR & TIMING
entries: The parts of the body that must be covered for salah and in situations where Islamic law requires covering.
Two prostrations of forgetfulness used to repair certain accidental mistakes involving wajib acts in salah.
A single prostration connected to designated Qur’an verses; it becomes wajib in Hanafi law when its conditions are met.
A prostration of gratitude to Allah after a major blessing or the removal of a calamity.
Making up an obligatory act of worship after its proper time has passed. In this deck it usually means a missed prayer.
The brief time when the sun is at its highest point, immediately before Dhuhr begins.
Recurring whisperings or intrusive doubts. In worship, this can mean doubts that should not be repeatedly fed or chased.

title: DAILY PRAYER NAMES
entries: The dawn prayer. It has 2 fard rak‘ahs.
The midday prayer after the sun passes its zenith. It has 4 fard rak‘ahs.
The afternoon prayer. It has 4 fard rak‘ahs; the Hanafi school uses its own relied-upon start-time calculation.
The sunset prayer. It has 3 fard rak‘ahs.
The night prayer after evening twilight disappears. It has 4 fard rak‘ahs.
An odd-numbered night prayer after Isha. In the Hanafi school it is 3 rak‘ahs and wajib.
The Friday congregational prayer that replaces Dhuhr for those upon whom it is obligatory.

title: VOLUNTARY PRAYER TERMS
entries: Voluntary night prayer, especially prayer offered after sleeping and then waking during the night.
Night worship after Isha and before Fajr. It is broader than Tahajjud.
Voluntary prayer near the beginning of the Duha time, after the sunrise restriction has ended.
Voluntary morning prayer after the sunrise restriction and before zawal.
A name used for recommended voluntary prayer after Maghrib; this deck follows the classical Hanafi six-rak‘ah practice.
Prayer and supplication asking Allah to guide you to what is good in a permissible choice.
A voluntary prayer connected with sincere repentance.
A voluntary prayer in which a person asks Allah for a lawful need.
A four-rak‘ah voluntary prayer containing repeated tasbih, 300 repetitions in the method used in this deck.

title: RAMADAN, EID & FUNERAL
entries: The ninth Islamic month, during which fasting is obligatory for Muslims who meet the conditions.
Fasting for Allah. In Ramadan this means abstaining from food, drink, and other fast-breakers from true dawn until sunset.
The Ramadan night prayer after Isha. The established Hanafi practice in this deck is 20 rak‘ahs.
The Night of Decree, a blessed night sought especially in the odd nights of Ramadan’s last ten nights.
The festival and Eid prayer marking the end of Ramadan.
The festival and Eid prayer during the Hajj season, associated with the sacrifice.
Funeral rites; in this deck the term usually means the funeral prayer for a deceased Muslim.
Gently prompting a dying Muslim to say La ilaha illallah without badgering the person.

title: TRAVEL & SPECIAL WORSHIP
entries: The pilgrimage to Makkah and its sacred sites performed in its appointed season by Muslims who are able.
Shortening the 4-rak‘ah fard prayers of Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha to 2 rak‘ahs for a qualifying Hanafi traveler.
The plain near Makkah where standing on the ninth day of the Hajj season is a central rite of Hajj.
A sacred Hajj site between ‘Arafah and Mina; Hanafi prayer-combining rules have a special Hajj exception there.
A solar eclipse. Salat al-Kusuf is the special prayer offered during a solar eclipse.
Seeking rain from Allah through repentance, du‘a, and, according to a recognized Hanafi position, a special prayer.
The prayer of fear: a special arrangement for obligatory prayer during serious armed danger.
